Yes—under those conditions, you would very likely be able to spot the Moon.

Why:

- **Altitude 5.3°**: It is low, only about a fist-width above the horizon at arm’s length, so buildings, hills, trees, haze, or a poor eastern/northeastern horizon could hide it. But if you have a clear view in that direction, it is genuinely above the geometric horizon.
- **Azimuth 59.7°**: Look roughly **east-northeast** (about 60° clockwise from north).
- **88% illuminated**: That is a bright waxing/waning gibbous Moon, easily visible to normal unaided vision.
- **Nautical twilight / Sun at −9.4°**: The sky is darkening substantially. Twilight will not prevent a nearly full Moon from being seen; if anything, it should stand out quite well once you look in the right place.
- **Clear sky**: This removes the main atmospheric obstacle, aside from the extra extinction and haze naturally present near the horizon.

So it is not guaranteed from every exact location—an obstructed or hazy ENE horizon could conceal it—but with an unobstructed clear horizon, you should be able to see it, probably as a conspicuous bright gibbous Moon low in the ENE.
